events.title: Adult Book Discussion: Theft
events.description: In November, the Cupertino Library Adult Book Discussion Group will talk about the 2022 novel Theft by Nobel Prize-winning author Abdulrazak Gurnah. Karim and Badar are two young men living on the East African island of Zanzibar. Karim's mother Raya leaves her abusive older husband when Karim is three, taking her son with her. However, when she finds a happy marriage with her new husband Haji Othman, Raya allows her parents to raise her son instead. Years later, when Karim is a university student living with his mother and stepfather for convenience, he meets and befriends the orphaned teenaged boy Badar, whose neglectful relatives force him to become a domestic servant in Haji Othmann's household. There, Badar is treated as a servant, although he is actually Othman's nephew. Fauzia, Karim's beautiful, studious girlfriend, teaches Badar the cooking and housekeeping skills he needs to become a successful domestic servant. Badar's fragile new security is abruptly destroyed when he is accused of theft and dismissed. Even though Karim helps him get a new job at a local hotel, things are never the same between them. The Adult Book Discussion Group meets twice a month, on the third Thursday morning at 11 am and on the third Thursday evening at 7 PM. Both meetings are held in Room 201B. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.blurb: Join the library's adult book group to talk through Abdulrazak Gurnah's 2022 novel Theft, which follows two young men living on Zanzibar.

stanfordSources.title: Book Talk — We Shall Outlast Them: Putin’s Global Campaign to Defeat the West
stanfordSources.description:
How has Russia sustained its confrontation with the West since 2022, and at what cost? In her new book, Hanna Notte argues the Kremlin is waging a war not only on Ukraine but over the global order itself.

Notte traces how Russia adapted after the invasion. It worked around sanctions, built new partnerships, cultivated support across the Global South and tried to deepen divisions within Western democracies. Her account combines policy analysis with field reporting from more than a dozen countries and interviews with officials, facilitators and ordinary people drawn into Russia's agenda.

The book also examines the domestic consequences. Notte finds that Putin's focus on confronting the West has distorted Russia's economy and moved the country from a tacit dictatorship toward a full one. She suggests Putin may outlast the West, but has gambled Russia's future in the process.

FSI Satre Family Senior Fellow and Mosbacher Director of CDDRL, Kathryn Stoner will moderate the discussion, which will cover Russian statecraft, the durability of autocratic regimes under pressure, and what Russia's strategy means for the U.S., Europe, and the Global South. Audience Q&A will follow.

ABOUT THE SPEAKER

Hanna Notte is the Director of the Eurasia Nonproliferation Program at the James Martin Center for Nonproliferation Studies. She is also a senior associate (non-resident) with the Center for Strategic and International Studies and with the Kennan Institute. Notte's expertise is in Russia's foreign and security policy. She holds a doctorate and Master's degree in international relations from Oxford University and a BA in social and political sciences from Cambridge University. During her doctoral studies, she was a visiting researcher with the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences and the Carnegie Moscow Center. Based in Berlin, she regularly writes for outlets such as the Financial Times, Foreign Affairs, the New York Times, and ZEIT, among others.

stanfordSources.title: Wellness Series: Elections Processing Space
stanfordSources.description:
Come stop by the A3C during Democracy Day! Counseling and Psychological Services (CAPS) Psychologist and Outreach Director Dr. Helen Hsu & the A3C will create a space for grounded reflections while offering wellness strategies for the election season. Dumplings will be provided as a light snack. Come hang out at the A3C Couchroom (Old Union Clubhouse, 2nd Floor) on November 3rd from 1:30 -3:30PM and be in community for the Wellness Series Election Processing Space. We can’t wait to see you there! 

Please RSVP by 11:59 PM PT on November 1st, 2026 so that we can plan accordingly: https://bit.ly/F26-elections
